topic.title: Why Rent Keeps Going Up
topic.hook: Supply, zoning, who sets the price
topic.payoff: Supply, zoning, who sets the price

copy.title: WHY YOUR RENT NEVER STOPS CLIMBING

steps.rule: Find who controls the land supply
steps.why: local governments cap how much housing can be built, which artificially tightens inventory before a single unit is priced.
rules that forbid dense building on most urban land guarantee that demand always outruns what developers are legally allowed to construct.

steps.rule: Track who votes on those rules
steps.why: existing property owners benefit directly when scarcity keeps values high, so the people who set the limits are the people who profit from them.
a city of one million renters needing two percent vacancy relief is twenty thousand units that current zoning may never permit to exist.

steps.rule: Name the feedback loop out loud
steps.why: higher rents lift assessed values, larger tax bases fund the councils that protect the zoning, and the machine resets at a higher floor every cycle.

copy.kicker: The price is a policy. Policies have authors.
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands upright on a plain white studio background, holding a single folded lease agreement in one hand and a red marker in the other, a small architectural zoning grid map resting against his leg on the floor, his expression sharp and direct, facing slightly toward camera.
copy.send_to: the friend renewing a lease and wondering why it jumped again
